articles.body: Every year the European Environment Agency publishes a remarkable open dataset: every new car registered in the EU , with its make, model, power, weight and official WLTP CO2 figure. It's a goldmine for anyone building with car data. In raw form, though, it's 10.7 million rows of inconsistent spellings, duplicates and provisional records. articles.body: Description A low-cost, serverless pipeline that streams, processes, stores, queries and alerts on stock data using AWS. Title Building a Near Real-Time Stock Analytics Pipeline on AWS Published false Tags aws, serverless, dataengineering, cloud I built a near real-time stock market analytics pipeline on AWS using an event-driven, serverless design. It ingests stock data, detects unusual movements, stores the results, and sends alerts, all while keeping costs low. How It Works Ingest: Stock data (e.g. from yfinance) is streamed into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process: AWS Lambda reads the stream, detects anomalies, and evaluates trends. Store (fast): Processed data goes to Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency lookups. Store (long-term): Raw data is archived in Amazon S3.

articles.title: Drawing Scale Conversion, Explained Simply (1:50, 1:100 & More)
articles.excerpt: Working with floor plans, blueprints or scale models means constantly translating between paper and real life. Here is the simple rule behind scale conversion. A scale is written as a ratio such as 1:…
articles.body: Working with floor plans, blueprints or scale models means constantly translating between paper and real life. Here is the simple rule behind scale conversion. What a scale ratio actually means A scale is written as a ratio such as 1:50 or 1:100. The first number is the distance on the drawing or model; the second is the same distance in the real world, in the same unit. 1:50 — 1 cm on the plan = 50 cm in reality. 1:100 — 1 cm on the plan = 100 cm (1 metre) in reality. 1:1,000 — 1 cm on a map = 1,000 cm (10 metres) on the ground. Converting a drawing measurement to real size Multiply the drawing measurement by the second number of the ratio. Example: a wall measures 24 mm on a 1:50 floor plan: 24 × 50 = 1,200 mm = 1.2 metres in real life.

articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. articles.body: NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life.
